title: Render presets in Rust: state the look and per-device wishes, test as a phone
note: Put the look and per-class wishes in genex.toml [render], never a fixed ultra; offer the settings panel; capture the game with renderSettings as mobile-mid and at low before calling it done.
intent: The renderer probes each device into a class (desktop-ultra to mobile-low; a browser from its own hints) and starts on that class's preset (low, medium, high, ultra); a dynamic-resolution controller steps the render scale to hold the class's frame time, and anything that does not fit the adapter or the class's memory budget turns cheaper or off and is listed in state().volatile.render.degraded by typed reason, never refused. A game states its look (tonemapper, exposure, bloom, fog, ao: equal everywhere) in [render.look] and, only where it matters, a class's quality in [render.class.<class>] (render_scale, fps, a feature switch such as bloom = false). Never hard-code ultra, a resolution or a render scale, never read render settings in a simulation hook, and make content cheap at low so presets add to it. Offer genex::render::settings_panel(ui) in an options menu: the person's choice is saved per device and never enters the Sim. Check the result the way a phone would draw it: renderSettings {set: {deviceClass: "mobile-mid"}} (then {set: {preset: "low"}}, {set: {features: {bloom: false}}}, {set: {renderScaleLock: 0.75}}, {set: {frameBudgetMs: 4}} so dynamic resolution holds a tight 4 ms and shows the stepped-down scale) and capture after each, since the answer's features describe the last drawn frame; the picture at low must still read as the same game. Captures are drawn on a pinned profile and settle their own history, so two runs of one build on one adapter give one picture. Give the game's own settings back with {set: {preset: null, features: null, deviceClass: null, renderScaleLock: null, frameBudgetMs: null}}.
port: The facet that owns the options menu owns the settings panel call; no other facet reads render settings.

evidence.note: Look and quality are separate; quality resolves class preset, then [render], then the person's panel choice, then the renderSettings verb; captures ignore the person's choice and settle on their own history.
The rules an agent follows: presets not numbers, the look in [render.look], built-ins before custom passes, test as mobile-mid and at low.
